findings.passage: This bill adds Concealed Weapons Permits to the acceptable forms of identification necessary in order for a voter to cast an electoral ballot. The common sense law gives voters yet another option to prove their identity at the polls and will only help expand the number of people able to vote in our elections.
findings.note: From his State House Report #14 (page publication date 2016-05-02), under the heading Adding CWP to Allowable Voter ID Forms. He describes a bill that adds the concealed weapons permit to the forms of ID accepted at the polls. Bill number is not printed in the passage.

findings.passage: This week, I voted in favor of legislation (H.3444) regarding our state’s election laws. This legislation has two goals: one, to maintain the integrity of each and every vote cast, and two, to ensure elections are run consistently across the state. After the elections of 2020, it became clear that there were discrepancies in the way each county handled votes. Simply put, we learned that counties were employing inconsistent processes, which is unacceptable. Upon ratification, this legislation would task the State Election Commission with ensuring there is a uniformity to guarantee free and fair elections. I supported this bill and it passed by a vote of 84-36.
findings.note: From his Legislative Update: Week 9, 2021 (heading: Maintaining the Integrity of our Elections). He explains his support for H. 3444 on election administration and uniform county procedures; the passage does not mention photo ID or citizenship.
